name: service-opentelemetry-web-vitals
title: Browser Web Vitals
description: An opt-in Web Vitals layer that reuses the browser OTLP event exporter and respects DNT/GPC.
docs:
## Overview

BrowserWebVitals collects document-level LCP, INP, CLS, FCP and TTFB through web-vitals and sends standard OTLP events. It depends on BrowserOtlp's event exporter; no SQL or application analytics service is required. Base BrowserOtlp and BrowserEvents entry points do not import this feature.

## Setup

```bash
bunx shadcn@latest add @krak-stack/service-opentelemetry-web-vitals
```

Package consumers import from `@krak-stack/registry/opentelemetry/web-vitals`. Enable OTLP logs export on the server, then compose browser telemetry:

```ts
import { Layer } from 'effect';
import { BrowserOtlp } from '@/services/opentelemetry/browser';
import { BrowserWebVitals } from '@/services/opentelemetry/web-vitals';

const telemetry = BrowserOtlp.layer({ serviceName: 'my-app-web' });
const browser = BrowserWebVitals.layer().pipe(
  Layer.provideMerge(telemetry),
);
```

Mount the composed layer in the browser runtime. Event export is enabled by default; BrowserOtlp owns batching and flushing. `events: false` disables all event export. This feature does not create an exporter.

To add analytics, install service-events and merge the collection layers before providing telemetry:

```ts
import { BrowserEvents } from '@/services/events/browser';

const browser = Layer.mergeAll(
  BrowserEvents.layer(),
  BrowserWebVitals.layer(),
).pipe(Layer.provideMerge(telemetry));
```

Both features share the exporter, but retain separate scopes. Web Vitals are generic telemetry, not application records stored in SQL.

## Privacy and lifetime

DNT/GPC disable collection by default. Use `BrowserWebVitals.layer({ respectDoNotTrack: false })` only when intentionally overriding those signals. The feature owns its privacy policy independently of BrowserEvents' enabled/analytics settings.

Closing the layer releases its subscription. Library observers are shared and document-scoped; remounting a layer does not register another set. Unsupported metrics may be absent. These are document metrics, not SPA navigation timings. No URLs, performance entries, DOM attribution or analytics identity/page context are exported automatically.

## Event format

Events follow the [OTel browser conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/browser/browser-events/): `browser.web_vital`, scope `krakstack.events`.

| Attribute | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `browser.web_vital.name` | Lowercase lcp/inp/cls/fcp/ttfb |
| `browser.web_vital.id` | Metric-instance ID |
| `browser.web_vital.value` | OTLP double; milliseconds except unitless CLS |
| `browser.web_vital.delta` | OTLP double since previous report |
| `browser.web_vital.rating` | good/needs-improvement/poor |
| `browser.web_vital.navigation_type` | Library navigation type |

Group by resource and metric ID. Use the latest cumulative value or sum deduplicated deltas, not cumulative values. Identical callbacks are suppressed; message IDs distinguish changed values but do not guarantee collector deduplication.
